package_info.package_manager: native (C/C++ library, used via system packages or bundled in binaries)
package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of libwebp contain a critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2023-4863/CVE-2023-5129) in the code that processes WebP images. This vulnerability allows attackers to execute arbitrary code when a crafted WebP image is processed, making any software using vulnerable libwebp versions susceptible to remote code execution attacks.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when processing a crafted WebP image)
execution_context.file_location: libwebp/src/demux/ (or equivalent image parsing code in the library)
required_permissions: potentially network (if image is received remotely)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a crafted WebP image is processed, the code allocates a buffer based on image dimensions and copies data from the image without proper bounds checking, leading to a heap buffer overflow and potential arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code fails to validate the size of the input data before copying it into a heap-allocated buffer, allowing an attacker to overwrite adjacent memory and potentially hijack program control flow.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Image parsing libraries are expected to strictly validate all input data and prevent memory corruption. This code violates that expectation by trusting untrusted image metadata.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate image decoders allocate buffers for image data, but must always validate input sizes.
key_indicators: Lack of bounds checking on memcpy/memmove
Buffer size derived from attacker-controlled image metadata

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious WebP image with manipulated metadata to trigger the buffer overflow.
attack_chain.leads_to: The image is delivered to a vulnerable application (e.g., via web upload, email, or messaging app).

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable application processes the malicious WebP image using libwebp.
attack_chain.leads_to: Heap buffer overflow occurs, allowing attacker-controlled code execution.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains arbitrary code execution in the context of the vulnerable application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential full system compromise, data theft, or further malware installation.

behavioral_signatures: Processing of WebP images leading to abnormal crashes or memory corruption
Unexpected application behavior after opening or previewing WebP files
Heap buffer overflows in image parsing routines
file_indicators: Presence of libwebp.so, libstatic-webp.so, libflutter.so in application packages
References to vulnerable libwebp versions in binaries or package manifests
system.new.dat files in firmware containing embedded libwebp
network_indicators: No direct network indicators from the vulnerability itself, but exploitation may result in outbound connections if attacker payload is executed
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan software and firmware for embedded libwebp libraries with versions prior to 1.3.2. Monitor for abnormal crashes or memory corruption when processing WebP images. Use static and dynamic analysis to identify unpatched libwebp code. Watch for applications that process WebP images from untrusted sources, and flag any heap buffer overflow events in image parsing routines.
